Let
\[
u(x)=\frac{1-\sqrt{1-4x^2}}2.
\]
Since \(u\) is even in \(x\), the main contribution as \(n\to\infty\) comes from \(x=0\). Put \(s=x^2\). Near \(0\),
\[
u(x)=s+s^2+2s^3+O(s^4),
\]
so the vertical width is
\[
u(x)-x^2=s^2+2s^3+O(s^4).
\]

Also, since \(y\sim x^2\) in the integration region,
\[
e^{-ny^2}=1-ny^2+O(n^2y^4).
\]
Thus
\[
\int_{x^2}^{u(x)} e^{-ny^2}\,dy
=(u-x^2)-\frac n3(u^3-x^6)+O(n^2x^{12}).
\]
Using \(u=x^2+O(x^4)\),
\[
u^3-x^6=3x^8+O(x^{10}),
\]
so
\[
\int_{x^2}^{u(x)} e^{-ny^2}\,dy
=x^4+2x^6-nx^8+O(x^8+nx^{10}+n^2x^{12}).
\]

Therefore
\[
M_n=\int_{-1/2}^{1/2}e^{-nx^2}(x^4+2x^6-nx^8)\,dx+O(n^{-9/2}).
\]
The Gaussian moment formula gives
\[
\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}x^4e^{-nx^2}\,dx=\frac{3\sqrt\pi}{4n^{5/2}},
\]
\[
\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}x^6e^{-nx^2}\,dx=\frac{15\sqrt\pi}{8n^{7/2}},
\qquad
\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}x^8e^{-nx^2}\,dx=\frac{105\sqrt\pi}{16n^{9/2}}.
\]
The tails outside \([-1/2,1/2]\) are exponentially small at this order, hence
\[
M_n=\frac{3\sqrt\pi}{4n^{5/2}}
+\left(2\cdot\frac{15\sqrt\pi}{8}-\frac{105\sqrt\pi}{16}\right)n^{-7/2}
+O(n^{-9/2}).
\]
The coefficient is
\[
\frac{30\sqrt\pi}{8}-\frac{105\sqrt\pi}{16}
=-\frac{45\sqrt\pi}{16}.
\]

\[
\boxed{-\frac{45\sqrt\pi}{16}}
\]
